extracted.intended_audience: public housing authorities (PHAs), owners of HUD-assisted housing, property managers, HUD field offices and inspectors
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards for physical-condition inspections, scoring, appeals, tenant notification, and uniform financial reporting for HUD-assisted housing and PHAs. Covers inspection frequencies, deficiency severity/timeframes, technical review/reinspection procedures, documentation and resident access, referral/enforcement triggers, and financial reporting submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 2 performing property designation and inspection frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: If a property receives a score of 80 points or higher but less than 90 on its physical condition inspection, the property will be designated a standard 2 performing property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties designated as standard 2 performing properties will be required to undergo a physical inspection once every two (2) years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 3 performing property designation and inspection frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: If a property receives a score of less than 80 points, the property will be designated a standard 3 performing property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties designated as standard 3 performing properties will continue to undergo an annual physical inspection as currently required under covered HUD programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial cycle for small rural PHAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Small rural PHAs as defined in 24 CFR 902.101 shall be assessed in accordance with part 902, subpart H of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small rural PHAs follow a triennial assessment/inspection cycle per the referenced regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial cycle for small PHAs (per 24 CFR 902.13(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Small PHAs as defined in 24 CFR 902.13(a) shall be assessed in accordance with 24 CFR 902.13(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment timing and methodology for small PHAs is governed by the cited provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection frequency for HCV units
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs must inspect units subject to part 982 of this title in accordance with the frequency described in 24 CFR 982.405.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HCV (tenant-based Section 8) inspections follow the frequency established in the HCV regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection frequency for project-based vouchers (PBV)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs must inspect units subject to 24 CFR part 983 in accordance with the frequency described in 24 CFR 983.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PBV inspection timing is controlled by the PBV regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection policy for FHA insured mortgages section 232 facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD may exempt assisted-living, board and care, and intermediate care facilities from physical inspections under this part if HUD determines that the State or local government has a reliable and adequate inspection system with results readily and timely available to HUD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other section 232 facilities, inspections will be conducted only when HUD determines—based on complaint, site inspection, or referral—that an inspection is needed to assure resident protection or adequate preservation of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection frequency for Section 8 Moderate Rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs must inspect units subject to the Moderate Rehabilitation program under 24 CFR part 882 in accordance with the frequency described in 24 CFR 882.516.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderate Rehabilitation program inspections follow the referenced regulation's frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection cost responsibility and reinspection fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of an inspection shall be the responsibility of the entity responsible for the inspection as identified in paragraph (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reasonable fee may be required of the owner for a reinspection if the owner notifies that a repair was made or the repair time elapsed and a reinspection shows the owner-responsible deficiency was not corrected. No fee may be charged to the household residing in the unit(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access requirement for HUD inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: All owners and PHAs are required to provide HUD or its representative with full and free access to all HUD-assisted properties and all units and appurtenances to permit physical inspections, monitoring reviews, and quality assurance reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access must be provided whether or not resident is home or if additional locks were installed without owner/PHA keys. Failure to provide access results in a physical condition score of zero for the project(s) involved; a score of zero is used to calculate the physical condition indicator and overall assessment score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant-initiated inspection recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will establish, through notice, a procedure for tenants to recommend particular units for HUD to inspect either during or separate from its standard inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD may evaluate these units and issue findings, but they will not be included in the official score unless they were randomly selected independent of the tenant's recommendation. Owners/PHAs must correct any deficiency HUD identifies within HUD-established timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual uniform self-inspection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All PHAs and owners of HUD housing subject to an assistance contract, other than owners participating in the HCV, PBV, and Moderate Rehabilitation programs, are required to annually self-inspect their properties, including all units, to ensure the units are maintained in accordance with the standards in § 5.703.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The owner or PHA must maintain self-inspection results for three years and provide results to HUD upon request. This self-inspection is independent of HUD inspections. The owner/PHA may choose to conduct it after a HUD inspection to satisfy both this requirement and the post-report survey requirement at § 5.711(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of inspection standards and scoring methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will publish in the Federal Register, following notice and opportunity to comment, a standards notification with a list of deficiencies and the relative severity and factors for determining pass/fail for certain programs; and a scoring notification containing methodologies for scoring and ranking HUD housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After considering public comments, the Secretary will publish documents announcing the new inspection standards/scoring methodologies and the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular revisions of inspection/scoring procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will issue a notification in the Federal Register published for at least 30 days of public comment making any revisions to inspection and scoring procedures HUD deems necessary, at least once every three years, or three years after the most recent revision, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions follow notice-and-comment unless emergency procedures are invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency revisions to inspection/scoring rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may publish a notification without 30 days of public comment in the case of an emergency to protect Federal financial resources or resident health/safety after HUD documents that such action is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency revisions are limited to documented life‑threatening or severe deficiencies, new safety concerns from changing construction technology, or other events as determined by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exclusions for scoring process
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative process for scoring and ranking the physical condition of HUD housing under this section does not apply to the HCV, PBV or Moderate Rehabilitation programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs administering HCV and PBV are assessed under SEMAP or small rural PHA assessment in 24 CFR part 985; PHAs administering Moderate Rehabilitation are subject to HUD review in accordance with 24 CFR 882.517.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity responsible for scoring and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD's Real Estate Assessment Center (REAC), or the appropriate entity as described in § 5.705(b) or as identified in the regulator agreement or contract, will score and rank the physical condition of HUD housing properties in accordance with procedures in § 5.709.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs operating public housing will be scored and ranked under PHAS as in part 902.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate notice and correction timeframe for Life‑Threatening and Severe deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion (or at end of each day on multi‑day inspection), REAC or inspecting party will provide the owner/PHA notice of any items classified as Life‑Threatening or Severe deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Life‑Threatening items must be corrected within 24 hours of receipt of notice unless HUD approves a variation. All Severe items must be corrected within 24 hours unless indicated otherwise in published inspection standards or HUD approves a variation. Owner/PHA must electronically certify and provide supporting evidence within 2 business days after the deadline that items have been resolved or hazard is blocked; if permanent repair will take longer, owner/PHA must provide HUD a timeframe for completing permanent repairs for HUD approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-report survey and correction timeframes for Moderate and Low deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or PHA must carefully review the inspection report and conduct its own survey. Moderate deficiencies must be corrected within thirty days and Low deficiencies within sixty days, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For properties scoring >= 60, the survey may be limited to inspecting for deficiencies based on the inspecting entity's findings. For properties scoring < 60, the owner/PHA must conduct a survey of the entire project (all units, inside/outside areas) and electronically submit the survey results to HUD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical review request deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a technical review of inspection results must be submitted electronically and must be received by the inspecting entity no later than the 45th calendar day following the day the inspection report is provided to the owner or PHA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted after 45 days are not timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and evidentiary standard for technical review
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must be accompanied by the owner/PHA's relevant evidence that an objectively verifiable and material error occurred or adverse conditions beyond owner/PHA control occurred which, if corrected, will result in a significant improvement in the overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical review will not be conducted based on conditions corrected after the inspection. REAC applies a rebuttable presumption that the inspection was conducted accurately. Acceptable evidence includes photographs, written material from objective subject-matter experts (e.g., fire marshal, building code official, registered architect or professional engineer), or similar evidence. Burden of proof rests with owner/PHA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available remedies from technical review
rubrics_metrics.description: If REAC determines that an objectively verifiable and material error or relevant adverse condition is documented and likely to result in significant improvement, REAC may: undertake a new inspection; correct the original inspection; or issue a new physical condition score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'new inspection' will be a complete reinspection and will constitute the final inspection for the project, producing a final inspection report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined bases for technical review / material errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Material errors or bases for adjustment include: (i) building data error (inspected wrong building), (ii) unit count error (incorrect total units due to HUD fault), (iii) non‑existent deficiency (recorded deficiency does not meet definition), (iv) adjustments for factors not reflected/inappropriately reflected (local code variance, elements not owned by project), (v) adjustments for adverse conditions beyond owner/PHA control (third‑party damage, natural disasters), and (vi) adjustments for modernization work in progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect data caused by owner/PHA failure to update HUD records cannot form the basis for review. Incorrect building data that does not affect score (e.g., address/name) is not material. Occupied units undergoing modernization are subject to inspection; deficiencies will be noted but owner/PHA may request an adjustment for work in progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of significant improvement for review purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant improvement refers to an increase in a score for the owner or PHA such that the new score crosses an administratively significant threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only score changes meeting this threshold will generally justify certain remedies and allocation of reinspection costs as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinspection scope when ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: If HUD determines a reinspection is appropriate, it will arrange for a complete reinspection of the project(s) in question, not just the previously identified deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reinspection will be the final inspection for the project and HUD will issue a final inspection report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent HUD review authority
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD may, absent an owner/PHA request for technical review, review inspection results that are anomalous or incorrect due to facts/circumstances not reflected properly in the inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD can initiate its own review when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of cost for new inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new inspection is undertaken and the new inspection results in a significant improvement, then the entity responsible for the inspection shall bear the expense of the new inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no significant improvement occurs, the owner or PHA responsible for the property must bear the expense. If paid by the owner/PHA, the cost is not an eligible project operating expense. The new inspection score is the final score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and publication of final scores
rubrics_metrics.description: The score of the property is the final score if the owner/PHA files no request for technical review or other adjustment; if review/adjustments occur, the final inspection score is the score issued by HUD after adjustments are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD will make public final scores through posting on HUD's internet site or other appropriate means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to residents of planned inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner or PHA must notify its residents of any planned inspections of their units or the housing development generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification timing and manner should ensure residents are aware of inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of inspection documents to residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final score has been issued the owner or PHA must make the physical inspection report and all related documents available to residents during regular business hours upon reasonable request for review and copying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related documents include the owner's/PHA's survey plan, plan of correction, certification, and related correspondence. After the final inspection score is published, any additional information (reinspection results, appeal requests) must be made available upon reasonable request. Documents must be maintained for resident review for 60 days from the date HUD provides the inspection score for the property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting notice of availability and meaningful access
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or PHA must post a notice to residents in the management office and on bulletin boards on the date of submission to the owner of the inspection score advising residents of the availability of inspection materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must be translated into other languages if necessary to provide meaningful access for limited English proficient individuals and should include HUD field office contact information where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident commenting and false certification reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Residents are encouraged to comment on information provided by the owner or PHA and submit comments directly to the applicable HUD field office or responsible entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If residents discover the owner or PHA provided HUD with a false certification during the review, they are encouraged to notify the applicable HUD field office for inquiry and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review triggers and DEC referral
rubrics_metrics.description: A property file receiving a score of 30 points or less, or two successive scores under 60, will be subject to additional administrative review; two successive scores under 60 may be referred to HUD's Departmental Enforcement Center (DEC). A score of 30 points or less is automatically referred to the DEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon referral, HUD will notify the owner/PHA; DEC evaluation may include input from tenants, HUD officials, elected officials, maintenance staff and others and may include a site visit. DEC may take enforcement action within delegated authority or recommend actions to HUD program offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of program office responsibilities during DEC evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: During DEC's evaluation period, HUD's program offices continue to be responsible for routine business, oversight, and monitoring; the mortgagee continues to carry out duties applicable to the mortgage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEC has primary responsibility for evaluation conclusions but works in consultation with program offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limitation on existing enforcement authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative process in this section does not prohibit HUD from taking any action necessary under existing statutes, regulations, contracts, grant agreements or other documents to protect HUD's interests and residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD may act notwithstanding commencement of the administrative scoring process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Uniform Financial Reporting Standards (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H implements uniform financial reporting standards for specified entities including PHAs receiving assistance under sections 5, 9, or 14 of the 1937 Act; PHAs as contract administrators for Section 8 programs; owners of Section 8 project-based housing; owners of multifamily projects receiving direct or indirect HUD assistance or with HUD-insured/held mortgages; HUD-approved lenders and investing mortgagees; and operators of projects with mortgages insured or held by HUD under section 232.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list includes many named HUD programs and mortgage categories; applicability is defined by the enumerated paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and submission requirements for financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities to which Subpart H applies must provide to HUD such financial information as required by HUD on an annual basis (except as required more frequently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be prepared in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (as defined by HUD), submitted electronically or in HUD-designated format (or non-electronic if HUD allows), and submitted in the form and substance prescribed by HUD. For section 232 properties, reports must also be submitted concurrently to the mortgagee in HUD-prescribed format/manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines for different entity types
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing deadlines vary by entity: (1) entities in paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) submit annually no later than 60 days after fiscal year end; (2) entities in (a)(3) and (a)(4) submit annually no later than 90 days after fiscal year end; (3) entities in (a)(5) submit annually no later than 90 days (with extension provisions); (4) entities in (a)(6) must submit quarterly and fiscal-year-to-date reports within 60 calendar days of each quarterly period deadline, with the final quarter within 90 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators in (a)(6) may opt for operator-certified rather than audited statements except if operator is also borrower; HUD may require audited statements if operator-certified info appears unreliable. HUD may request more frequent statements case-by-case and can obtain more information under regulatory agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting compliance start dates and transitional provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities must commence compliance per specified dates depending on entity type (examples: PHAs with fiscal years ending Sept 30, 1999 and later; other entities with fiscal years ending Dec 31, 1998 and later; lenders with fiscal years on or after Sept 30, 2002; entities in (a)(6) after HUD issues guidance on transmission methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional allowances exist for entities electing to submit earlier; audited vs. unaudited requirements track statutory authorities like Single Audit Act and 2 CFR part 200.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on changing fiscal years for PHAs
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs listed in paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) will not be allowed to change their fiscal years for their first three full fiscal years following October 1, 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation is to allow consistent assessment of financial reports submitted to HUD under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for submission of financial reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility for submission of the financial report due to HUD rests with the individuals and entities listed in paragraph (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must ensure timely, complete, and accurate submission as prescribed.
